Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿And by the night and what it gathers (wa sa)﴾ (84:17), that he said: what enters into it.

Abu 'Ubayd in his Fada'il, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him concerning ﴿wa sa﴾ that he said: what it gathers.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also concerning His words, ﴿And by the moon when it becomes full (ittasaqa)﴾ (84:18), that he said: when it becomes equal (istawa).

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Anbari narrated through several chains from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about His words, ﴿And by the night and what it gathers﴾, and he said: what it gathers. Have you not heard the saying of the poet:

"Indeed we have she-camels, fat and spirited,
gathering together, if only they found a driver."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from him concerning ﴿And by the moon when it becomes full﴾ that he said: the night of the thirteenth.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab concerning ﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾ (84:19): state after state. al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾: state after state. He said: this is your Prophet ﷺ.

Abu 'Ubayd in al-Qira'at, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mani', 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite "la-tarkabanna tabaqan 'an tabaq", meaning with a fatha on the ba' of tarkabanna.

He also said: meaning your Prophet ﷺ, state after state.

al-Tayalisi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated from him that he said: "la-tarkabanna", O Muhammad, the sky, stage after stage.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, al-Tabarani, Ibn Manda and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited "la-tarkabanna", meaning with a fatha on the ba'.

He also said: la-tarkabanna, O Muhammad, sama'an ba'da sama'in (heaven after heaven).

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from him concerning ﴿la-tarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: he said: meaning the sky will be split, then torn, then reddened.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him also concerning the verse, that he said: the sky will be like molten metal (al-muhl), and it will be like red rose, like oil (al-dihan), and it will be fragile, and it will be split open, so it will be state after state.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾, that he said: they keep it secret.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 84, verses 1–25 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan without any disagreement.

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Surat al-Inshiqaq was revealed at Mecca."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn al-Zubayr something similar.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others related from Abu Rafiʿ, who said: "I prayed with Abu Hurayrah the ʿatamah (night prayer), and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated. I said to him about it, and he said: 'I prostrated behind Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ), and I will not cease to prostrate in it until I meet him.'"

Muslim, the authors of the Sunan and others related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "We prostrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾" [i.e., Surat al-ʿAlaq].

Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Ruwayani in his Musnad, and al-Diya al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtarah related from Buraydah that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the noon prayer ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and similar to it."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ is like His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ (al-Takwir: 1) regarding the presence and absence of an implied verb.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: Its splitting is one of the signs of the Resurrection, and the meaning of its splitting is its cleaving with white clouds, as in His saying ﴿And the day the sky is split open with clouds﴾ (al-Furqan: 25). It was also said that it splits from the Milky Way, and the Milky Way is a gate of the sky.

The answer (jawab) of ("idha") has been disputed. al-Farraʾ said that it is "adhinat" (listened), and the waw is extra, and likewise "alqat" (cast out).

Ibn al-Anbari said: This is an error, because the Arabs do not insert the waw except with "hatta idha", as in His saying ﴿until, when they came to it and its gates were opened﴾ (al-Zumar: 73), and with "lamma", as in His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted and he had put him down upon his temple﴾ and ﴿And We called to him﴾ (al-Saffat: 103–104). It is not inserted with other than these two.

It was also said that the answer is His saying "fa-mulaqihi," meaning "then you will meet it," and this was the view of al-Akhfash.

al-Mubarrad said: In the speech there is a transposition: that is, ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor and will meet Him﴾ ﴿When the sky is split open﴾.

al-Mubarrad also said: The answer is His saying ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾, and this was the view of al-Kisaʾi. The estimate is: ﴿When the sky is split open﴾, then whoever is given his record in his right hand, his ruling is such-and-such. It was also said that it is "O mankind" with an implied "fa" (then). It was said that it is "O mankind" with an implied "qawl" (saying): that is, it is said to him, "O mankind." It was also said that the answer is omitted, its estimate being (you will be resurrected), or (every human will meet his deed). It was also said that it is what was explicitly stated in Surat al-Takwir: that is, ("a soul will know this"), on the assumption that "idha" is conditional. It was also said that it is not conditional, and is in the accusative governed by an omitted verb, meaning: remember. Or it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is the second "idha," and the waw is extra, its estimate being: the time of the splitting of the sky is the time of the stretching of the earth.

The meaning of ﴿and it has listened to its Lord﴾ is that it obeyed Him in splitting, from "idhn," which is listening to a thing and giving ear to it. ﴿And it has been right to do so﴾ means: it is right for it to obey, submit and listen. Among the uses of "idhn" in the sense of listening is the saying of the poet:

"Deaf when they hear good spoken of me, and if I am mentioned with evil in their presence, they listen (adhinu)."

And the saying of another:

"If they listen to a suspicion, they fly with it, rejoicing at me; and if they listen to something righteous, they are buried."

It was also said that the meaning is: Allah made it obligatory upon it to listen to His command to split: that is, He made it deserving of that.

al-Dahhak said: "Haqqat" means it obeyed, and it is right for it to obey its Lord because He created it. It is said: "So-and-so is entitled (mahquq) to such-and-such." The meaning of its obedience is that it does not refuse what Allah wills for it.

Qatadah said: "Haqqa laha" means it is right for it to do that. From this is the saying of Kuthayyir:

"If there is reproach, then welcome and well-come; and reproach has been due to them with us, and has become little."

And ﴿when the earth is stretched out﴾, that is, spread out as hides are spread, and its mountains are leveled until it becomes a smooth plain in which you see no crookedness or elevation.

Muqatil said: It is made level like the stretching of a hide, so no building and no mountain remains upon it except that it enters into it. It was also said: "Maddat" means it is increased in its extent, from "madad," which is increase.

﴿And it casts out what is within it﴾, that is, it brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, and throws them onto its surface, and empties itself of that.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: It casts out what is in its belly of the dead, and empties itself of those who are on its back of the living. A similar thing is His saying ﴿And the earth will bring forth its burdens﴾ (al-Zalzalah: 2).

﴿And it has listened to its Lord﴾, that is, it heard and obeyed in what He commanded it of casting out and emptying, and ﴿it has been right to do so﴾, that is, it was made deserving of listening to that and submitting to it. The meanings of the two verbs have already been explained before this.

﴿O mankind﴾: the intended meaning is the species of mankind, so it includes the believer and the disbeliever. It was also said that it means the disbelieving human. The first is preferable because of what follows of the detail. ﴿Indeed, you are laboring toward your Lord with labor﴾. "Kadh" in the speech of the Arabs means striving at a thing with effort, without distinction whether that thing is good or evil. The meaning is: indeed you are striving toward your Lord in your deeds, or toward meeting your Lord. It is derived from "kadaha jildahu," when he scratched his skin.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"Time is but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek life, laboring."

Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: "Workers for your Lord with a deed, and you will meet it," meaning: you will meet your deed. The meaning is that he will inevitably meet the reward of his deed and what follows from it of reward and punishment.

al-Qutaybi said: The meaning of the verse is: indeed you are laboring, that is, a worker toiling in your livelihood, toward the meeting with your Lord. "Mulaqah" means "liqa," that is, you will meet your Lord with your deed. It was also said: "fa-mulaqin kitaba ʿamalika" (you will meet the record of your deed), because the deed has already ended.

﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾: and they are the believers.

﴿He will be judged with an easy account﴾, without any scrutiny.

Muqatil said: Because his sins will be forgiven and he will not be called to account for them.

The exegetes said: It is that his sins are presented to him, then Allah forgives them, and that is the easy account.

﴿And he will return to his family in joy﴾: that is, after the easy account he will turn to his family who are in Paradise from among his kin, or to his family who were with him in the world of wives and children and who had preceded him to Paradise, or to those whom Allah prepared for him in Paradise of the wide-eyed houris and the everlasting youths, or to all of these, rejoicing, delighted with what he was given of good and honor.

﴿But as for he who is given his record behind his back﴾. al-Kalbi said: Because his right hand is chained to his neck, and his left hand will be behind him.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: The plates of his chest and his bones will be unlocked, then his hand will enter and come out from his back, and he will take his record in that manner.

﴿He will call for destruction﴾: that is, when he reads his record he will say: "Woe to me! Destruction to me!" And "thubur" means ruin.

﴿And he will burn in the Blaze﴾: that is, he will enter it and endure its heat and its severity.

Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah and ʿAsim read with a fatha on the ya and a sukun on the sad and a light lam.

The rest read with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the lam with a shadda. Ismaʿil al-Makki related from Ibn Kathir, and likewise Kharijah from Nafiʿ, and likewise Ismaʿil al-Makki related from Ibn Kathir that they read with a damma on the ya and a sukun on the sad, from "asla, yuslee."

﴿Indeed, he was among his people in joy﴾: that is, he was among his people in the world, rejoicing in following his desires and riding his lust, insolent and exultant, because the Hereafter did not occur to his mind. The clause is an explanation of what precedes it.

The clause ﴿Indeed, he thought that he would never return﴾ is an explanation of his being joyful among his people in the world. The meaning: the cause of that joy was his thinking that he would not return to Allah and would not be raised for reckoning and punishment, because he denied the resurrection and rejected the Hereafter. In His saying "an lan yahur," "an" is the light form of the heavy one, and together with what follows it fills the place of the two objects of "thanna." "Hawr" in the language means returning. It is said: "haara yahuru," when he returned. al-Raghib said: "Hawr" is hesitation in a matter, and from it: "We seek refuge in Allah from hawr after kawr," that is, from hesitation in a matter after proceeding in it. "Muhawarat al-kalam" is reviewing the speech, and "mahar" is the return and destination.

ʿIkrimah and Dawud ibn Abi Hind said: "Yahur" is a word in Abyssinian, and its meaning is "he returns."

al-Qurtubi said: "Hawr" in the speech of the Arabs means return, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hawr after kawr," meaning from returning to deficiency after increase. Likewise "hur" with a damma. In the proverb: "hur fi mahar," that is, a deficiency upon a deficiency. From it is the saying of the poet:

"The blood is shed, and the people's returner is in hur."

"Hur" also means destruction, and from it is the saying of the rajiz:

"In a well without hur he traveled, and he did not perceive."

Abu ʿUbaydah said: That is, in a well of hur, and "la" is extra.

﴿Yes, indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him﴾. "Bala" is an affirmation of the negated with "lan": that is, yes, he will surely return and will surely be raised.

Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him, that is, He was knowing of him and of his deeds, nothing of them hidden from Him.

al-Zajjaj said: "Kana bihi basiran" means He was knowing of him before He created him, knowing that his return would be to Him.

﴿So I swear by the twilight﴾: "la" is extra, as was mentioned before in similar expressions, and we have already mentioned the disagreement about it in Surat al-Qiyamah, so return to it. "Shafaq" is the redness that is after the setting of the sun until the time of the late night prayer (al-ʿIshaʾ).

al-Wahidi said: This is the view of the exegetes and the people of the language all together.

al-Farraʾ said: I heard some of the Arabs say: "Upon him is a garment dyed as if it were the shafaq," and it was red.

al-Qurtubi related this from most of the Companions, the Successors and the jurists.

Asad ibn ʿUmar and Abu Hanifah, in one of the two reports from him, said: It is whiteness. There is no basis for this view, nor any support for it, neither from the language of the Arabs nor from the Law.

al-Khalil said: "Shafaq" is the redness from the setting of the sun, and its redness at the beginning of the night until near the late night prayer. The books of language and of the Law agree upon this, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"Arise, O boy, help me, not hesitating, over time, with a cup whose filling is shafaq."

And another said:

"Of red hue like the redness of the shafaq."

Mujahid said: "Shafaq" is all of the daytime. Do you not see that He said: "and the night and what it gathers"? ʿIkrimah said: It is what remains of the daytime. They only said this because of His saying after it, "and the night and what it gathers," as if He swore by the light and the darkness. But there is no basis for this. Yet it has been related from ʿIkrimah that he said: "Shafaq" is what is between the sunset and the ʿIshaʾ. And it has been related from Asad ibn ʿUmar: "The return."

"And the night and what it gathers": "al-wasq" in the view of the people of the language is the joining of one thing to another. It is said: "istawsaqat al-ibil," when the camels gathered and came together, and "al-raʿi yasiquha," that is, he gathers them.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes say: "wa-ma wasaq" means what gathers, joins, contains and wraps. The meaning is that it gathers and joins what was scattered during the day in its activity, because when the night comes every thing returns to its shelter. From it is the saying of Dabiʾ ibn al-Harith al-Burjumi:

"So I and you, and driving toward you, are like one who grasps a thing that his fingers have not reached."

ʿIkrimah said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what drives anything to where it shelters, so he made it from "sawq" (driving), not from gathering. It was also said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what hides and covers. It was also said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what carries. Everything you carry, you have "wasaqtahu." The Arabs say: "I will not carry it, what my eye has carried of water," that is, it carried it. And the she-camel "wasaqat tasiqu wasqan," that is, carried.

Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what carries of darkness, or carries of the stars.

al-Qushayri said: The meaning of "hamala" is gathering and joining, and the night by its darkness carries every thing.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what is done in it of night prayer and seeking forgiveness at dawn. The first is preferable.

﴿And the moon when it becomes full﴾, that is, it gathers and is complete.

al-Farraʾ said: Its "ittisaq" is its becoming full, its gathering and its evening out, on the thirteenth and fourteenth night until the sixteenth. It is derived from "al-wasq," which is gathering.

al-Hasan said: "Ittasaqa" means it became full and gathered.

Qatadah said: It became round. It is said: "wasaqtuhu fa-ittasaq," as it is said: "wasaltuhu fa-ittasal" (I joined him and he became joined). And it is said: "amr fulan muttasiq," that is, gathered and ordered. And it is said: "ittasaqa al-shayʾ" when it follows in succession.

﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾: this is the answer to the oath.

Qur'an 84:19 is read with a fatha on the ba' (la-tarkabanna) by Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr, as addressed to one person, namely the Prophet ﷺ, or to anyone who is fit for it. This is also the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Masruq, Abu Wa'il, Mujahid, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. The rest read it with a damma on the ba', as addressed to the plural, meaning mankind.

al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: "La-tarkabanna, O Muhammad, sama'an ba'da sama'in" (you will ascend heaven after heaven). al-Kalbi said: "It means you will climb through them." This is according to the first reading. It was also said: a rank after a rank and a station after a station in nearness to Allah and elevation of status. It was also said that the meaning is: you will pass through state after state, each state resembling its sister in severity. It was also said that the meaning is: O human being, you will pass through state after state, from being a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then living and dead, and rich and poor. In this case the address is to the human being mentioned in His words, ﴿O mankind, indeed you are labouring toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾ (84:6). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose the second reading. They said: "Because the meaning concerning mankind is more fitting than the meaning concerning the Prophet ﷺ."

'Umar read "la-yarkabanna" with a ya' at the beginning and a damma on the ba', as a report. It is narrated from him and from Ibn 'Abbas that they read it in the third person with a fatha on the ba', meaning la-yarkabanna al-insanu (mankind will pass through). It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas that they read the prefix vowel with a kasra, and this is a dialectal form. It was also read with a fatha on the prefix and a kasra on the ba', as addressed to the self (nafs).

It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: the moon will pass through states of waning and of new crescent. This is far-fetched.

Muqatil said: "tabaqan 'an tabaq" means death and life.

'Ikrimah said: a suckling infant, then a weaned child, then a youth, then a young man, then an old man.

The position of 'an tabaq in the accusative is either as a description of tabaqan, meaning a stage passing beyond another stage, or as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the pronoun in la-tarkabanna, meaning passing beyond, or passing beyond one another.

﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ (84:20). The interrogative is for denial, and the fa' (so) indicates the sequence of the denial and astonishment that follows what precedes it, concerning the events of the Day of Resurrection or other matters, according to the earlier disagreement. The meaning is: what is the matter with the disbelievers that they do not believe in Muhammad ﷺ and in what he brought of the Qur'an, when the causes of belief in it are present?

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate﴾ (84:21). This conditional clause and its response are in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). The meaning is: what prevents them, at the time of not prostrating and humbling themselves when the Qur'an is recited?

al-Hasan, 'Ata', al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: "What is wrong with them that they do not pray?"

Abu Muslim said: the intended meaning is humility and submission.

It was also said that the intended meaning is the prostration itself known as the prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawah).

There has been disagreement as to whether this place is one of the places of prostration during recitation or not. The evidence for prostration was already mentioned at the beginning of this surah.

﴿Rather, those who disbelieve deny﴾ (84:22). That is, they deny Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought of the Book, which includes affirmation of monotheism, resurrection, reward and punishment.

﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾ (84:23). That is, of what they hide within themselves of denial. Muqatil said: they conceal some of their deeds.

Ibn Zayd said: they gather good and bad deeds. It is derived from the wi'a (receptacle) in which what is within it is gathered. From this is the poet's saying:

"Goodness endures, though time be long upon it,
and evil is the worst of what you store as provision."

It is said: wa'a means he preserved it, and I heard the hadith (wa'aytu al-hadith a'ihi wa'yan), and from this is ﴿an attentive ear﴾ (69:12).

﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (84:24). That is, treat that as glad tidings for them, because His knowledge, glorified is He, of that in the manner mentioned necessitates their punishment. The painful (alim) is that which causes pain and is afflicting. The statement is in the form of mockery toward them.

﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted﴾ (84:25). This exception is disjunctive (istithna' munqati'). That is, but those who combine belief in Allah with righteous action, for them is a reward with Allah that is not cut off (ghayr mamnun), that is, not severed. It is said: manantu al-habl, meaning I cut the rope. From this is the poet's saying:

"You see behind them, from the speed of the camels, dust like the scattering of motes."

al-Mubarrad said: al-manin is dust, because it cuts through the air behind them. Every weak thing is manin and mamnun. It was also said that the meaning of ghayr mamnun is that it is not bestowed upon them as a favour. It is permissible for the exception to be connected (muttasil) if what is meant is those among them who believed.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib concerning His words, ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ (84:1), that he said: the sky splits from the Milky Way.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿And it has listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ (84:2) that he said: it heard when He spoke to it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also concerning ﴿And it has listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ that he said: it obeyed, and it was obligated by obedience.

al-Hakim narrated from him and declared it sound, that he said: it heard and obeyed. ﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾ (84:3): he said: on the Day of Resurrection, and it casts out what is in it: he said: it brings out what is in it of the dead and empties itself of them.

Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him concerning ﴿and casts out what is in it﴾ that he said: the gold bracelets.

al-Hakim narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a good chain, from Jabir who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The earth will be stretched out on the Day of Resurrection like the stretching of a hide, and then there will be for the son of Adam in it only the place of his two feet."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with toil﴾ (84:6) that he said: one who works a deed and will encounter it; he said: one who will encounter your deed.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from 'A'ishah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one is called to account but he will be destroyed." I said: "Does Allah not say: ﴿Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾ ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾ (84:7–8)?" He said: "That is not the reckoning, but that is the presentation (al-'ard). Whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be destroyed."

Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh (p. 1603) narrated from 'A'ishah who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say in some of his prayer: 'O Allah, call me to a light account.' When he finished, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the light account?' He said: 'That he looks into his record and He overlooks it for him. Indeed whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be destroyed.'" In some wordings of the first hadith and this other hadith: "Whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be punished."

al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Bayhaqi and al-Hakim narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Three whoever has them, Allah will call him to a light reckoning and admit him to Paradise by His mercy: you give to one who withholds from you, you pardon one who wronged you, and you join one who cut you off."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿He called out for destruction﴾ (84:11), that he said: the woe (al-wayl).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him concerning His words, ﴿that he thought he would never return﴾ (84:14), that he said: he will be resurrected.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning ﴿that he would never return﴾, that he said: that he would never go back.

Sammawayh narrated in his Fawa'id from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: "al-Shafaq" is the redness.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated the same from Ibn 'Abbas.

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: "al-Shafaq" is the whole of the day.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿And by the night and what it gathers (wa sa)﴾ (84:17), that he said: what enters into it.

Abu 'Ubayd in his Fada'il, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him concerning ﴿wa sa﴾ that he said: what it gathers.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also concerning His words, ﴿And by the moon when it becomes full (ittasaqa)﴾ (84:18), that he said: when it becomes equal (istawa).

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Anbari narrated through several chains from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about His words, ﴿And by the night and what it gathers﴾, and he said: what it gathers. Have you not heard the saying of the poet:

"Indeed we have she-camels, fat and spirited,
gathering together, if only they found a driver."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from him concerning ﴿And by the moon when it becomes full﴾ that he said: the night of the thirteenth.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab concerning ﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾ (84:19): state after state. al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾: state after state. He said: this is your Prophet ﷺ.

Abu 'Ubayd in al-Qira'at, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mani', 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite "la-tarkabanna tabaqan 'an tabaq", meaning with a fatha on the ba' of tarkabanna.

He also said: meaning your Prophet ﷺ, state after state.

al-Tayalisi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated from him that he said: "la-tarkabanna", O Muhammad, the sky, stage after stage.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, al-Tabarani, Ibn Manda and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited "la-tarkabanna", meaning with a fatha on the ba'.

He also said: la-tarkabanna, O Muhammad, sama'an ba'da sama'in (heaven after heaven).

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from him concerning ﴿la-tarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: he said: meaning the sky will be split, then torn, then reddened.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him also concerning the verse, that he said: the sky will be like molten metal (al-muhl), and it will be like red rose, like oil (al-dihan), and it will be fragile, and it will be split open, so it will be state after state.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾, that he said: they keep it secret.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 84, verses 1–25 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan without any disagreement.

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Surat al-Inshiqaq was revealed at Mecca."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn al-Zubayr something similar.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others related from Abu Rafiʿ, who said: "I prayed with Abu Hurayrah the ʿatamah (night prayer), and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated. I said to him about it, and he said: 'I prostrated behind Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ), and I will not cease to prostrate in it until I meet him.'"

Muslim, the authors of the Sunan and others related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "We prostrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾" [i.e., Surat al-ʿAlaq].

Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Ruwayani in his Musnad, and al-Diya al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtarah related from Buraydah that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the noon prayer ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and similar to it."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ is like His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ (al-Takwir: 1) regarding the presence and absence of an implied verb.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: Its splitting is one of the signs of the Resurrection, and the meaning of its splitting is its cleaving with white clouds, as in His saying ﴿And the day the sky is split open with clouds﴾ (al-Furqan: 25). It was also said that it splits from the Milky Way, and the Milky Way is a gate of the sky.

The answer (jawab) of ("idha") has been disputed. al-Farraʾ said that it is "adhinat" (listened), and the waw is extra, and likewise "alqat" (cast out).

Ibn al-Anbari said: This is an error, because the Arabs do not insert the waw except with "hatta idha", as in His saying ﴿until, when they came to it and its gates were opened﴾ (al-Zumar: 73), and with "lamma", as in His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted and he had put him down upon his temple﴾ and ﴿And We called to him﴾ (al-Saffat: 103–104). It is not inserted with other than these two.

It was also said that the answer is His saying "fa-mulaqihi," meaning "then you will meet it," and this was the view of al-Akhfash.

al-Mubarrad said: In the speech there is a transposition: that is, ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor and will meet Him﴾ ﴿When the sky is split open﴾.

al-Mubarrad also said: The answer is His saying ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾, and this was the view of al-Kisaʾi. The estimate is: ﴿When the sky is split open﴾, then whoever is given his record in his right hand, his ruling is such-and-such. It was also said that it is "O mankind" with an implied "fa" (then). It was said that it is "O mankind" with an implied "qawl" (saying): that is, it is said to him, "O mankind." It was also said that the answer is omitted, its estimate being (you will be resurrected), or (every human will meet his deed). It was also said that it is what was explicitly stated in Surat al-Takwir: that is, ("a soul will know this"), on the assumption that "idha" is conditional. It was also said that it is not conditional, and is in the accusative governed by an omitted verb, meaning: remember. Or it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is the second "idha," and the waw is extra, its estimate being: the time of the splitting of the sky is the time of the stretching of the earth.

The meaning of ﴿and it has listened to its Lord﴾ is that it obeyed Him in splitting, from "idhn," which is listening to a thing and giving ear to it. ﴿And it has been right to do so﴾ means: it is right for it to obey, submit and listen. Among the uses of "idhn" in the sense of listening is the saying of the poet:

"Deaf when they hear good spoken of me, and if I am mentioned with evil in their presence, they listen (adhinu)."

And the saying of another:

"If they listen to a suspicion, they fly with it, rejoicing at me; and if they listen to something righteous, they are buried."

It was also said that the meaning is: Allah made it obligatory upon it to listen to His command to split: that is, He made it deserving of that.

al-Dahhak said: "Haqqat" means it obeyed, and it is right for it to obey its Lord because He created it. It is said: "So-and-so is entitled (mahquq) to such-and-such." The meaning of its obedience is that it does not refuse what Allah wills for it.

Qatadah said: "Haqqa laha" means it is right for it to do that. From this is the saying of Kuthayyir:

"If there is reproach, then welcome and well-come; and reproach has been due to them with us, and has become little."

And ﴿when the earth is stretched out﴾, that is, spread out as hides are spread, and its mountains are leveled until it becomes a smooth plain in which you see no crookedness or elevation.

Muqatil said: It is made level like the stretching of a hide, so no building and no mountain remains upon it except that it enters into it. It was also said: "Maddat" means it is increased in its extent, from "madad," which is increase.

﴿And it casts out what is within it﴾, that is, it brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, and throws them onto its surface, and empties itself of that.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: It casts out what is in its belly of the dead, and empties itself of those who are on its back of the living. A similar thing is His saying ﴿And the earth will bring forth its burdens﴾ (al-Zalzalah: 2).

﴿And it has listened to its Lord﴾, that is, it heard and obeyed in what He commanded it of casting out and emptying, and ﴿it has been right to do so﴾, that is, it was made deserving of listening to that and submitting to it. The meanings of the two verbs have already been explained before this.

﴿O mankind﴾: the intended meaning is the species of mankind, so it includes the believer and the disbeliever. It was also said that it means the disbelieving human. The first is preferable because of what follows of the detail. ﴿Indeed, you are laboring toward your Lord with labor﴾. "Kadh" in the speech of the Arabs means striving at a thing with effort, without distinction whether that thing is good or evil. The meaning is: indeed you are striving toward your Lord in your deeds, or toward meeting your Lord. It is derived from "kadaha jildahu," when he scratched his skin.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"Time is but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek life, laboring."

Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: "Workers for your Lord with a deed, and you will meet it," meaning: you will meet your deed. The meaning is that he will inevitably meet the reward of his deed and what follows from it of reward and punishment.

al-Qutaybi said: The meaning of the verse is: indeed you are laboring, that is, a worker toiling in your livelihood, toward the meeting with your Lord. "Mulaqah" means "liqa," that is, you will meet your Lord with your deed. It was also said: "fa-mulaqin kitaba ʿamalika" (you will meet the record of your deed), because the deed has already ended.

﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾: and they are the believers.

﴿He will be judged with an easy account﴾, without any scrutiny.

Muqatil said: Because his sins will be forgiven and he will not be called to account for them.

The exegetes said: It is that his sins are presented to him, then Allah forgives them, and that is the easy account.

﴿And he will return to his family in joy﴾: that is, after the easy account he will turn to his family who are in Paradise from among his kin, or to his family who were with him in the world of wives and children and who had preceded him to Paradise, or to those whom Allah prepared for him in Paradise of the wide-eyed houris and the everlasting youths, or to all of these, rejoicing, delighted with what he was given of good and honor.

﴿But as for he who is given his record behind his back﴾. al-Kalbi said: Because his right hand is chained to his neck, and his left hand will be behind him.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: The plates of his chest and his bones will be unlocked, then his hand will enter and come out from his back, and he will take his record in that manner.

﴿He will call for destruction﴾: that is, when he reads his record he will say: "Woe to me! Destruction to me!" And "thubur" means ruin.

﴿And he will burn in the Blaze﴾: that is, he will enter it and endure its heat and its severity.

Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah and ʿAsim read with a fatha on the ya and a sukun on the sad and a light lam.

The rest read with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the lam with a shadda. Ismaʿil al-Makki related from Ibn Kathir, and likewise Kharijah from Nafiʿ, and likewise Ismaʿil al-Makki related from Ibn Kathir that they read with a damma on the ya and a sukun on the sad, from "asla, yuslee."

﴿Indeed, he was among his people in joy﴾: that is, he was among his people in the world, rejoicing in following his desires and riding his lust, insolent and exultant, because the Hereafter did not occur to his mind. The clause is an explanation of what precedes it.

The clause ﴿Indeed, he thought that he would never return﴾ is an explanation of his being joyful among his people in the world. The meaning: the cause of that joy was his thinking that he would not return to Allah and would not be raised for reckoning and punishment, because he denied the resurrection and rejected the Hereafter. In His saying "an lan yahur," "an" is the light form of the heavy one, and together with what follows it fills the place of the two objects of "thanna." "Hawr" in the language means returning. It is said: "haara yahuru," when he returned. al-Raghib said: "Hawr" is hesitation in a matter, and from it: "We seek refuge in Allah from hawr after kawr," that is, from hesitation in a matter after proceeding in it. "Muhawarat al-kalam" is reviewing the speech, and "mahar" is the return and destination.

ʿIkrimah and Dawud ibn Abi Hind said: "Yahur" is a word in Abyssinian, and its meaning is "he returns."

al-Qurtubi said: "Hawr" in the speech of the Arabs means return, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hawr after kawr," meaning from returning to deficiency after increase. Likewise "hur" with a damma. In the proverb: "hur fi mahar," that is, a deficiency upon a deficiency. From it is the saying of the poet:

"The blood is shed, and the people's returner is in hur."

"Hur" also means destruction, and from it is the saying of the rajiz:

"In a well without hur he traveled, and he did not perceive."

Abu ʿUbaydah said: That is, in a well of hur, and "la" is extra.

﴿Yes, indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him﴾. "Bala" is an affirmation of the negated with "lan": that is, yes, he will surely return and will surely be raised.

Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him, that is, He was knowing of him and of his deeds, nothing of them hidden from Him.

al-Zajjaj said: "Kana bihi basiran" means He was knowing of him before He created him, knowing that his return would be to Him.

﴿So I swear by the twilight﴾: "la" is extra, as was mentioned before in similar expressions, and we have already mentioned the disagreement about it in Surat al-Qiyamah, so return to it. "Shafaq" is the redness that is after the setting of the sun until the time of the late night prayer (al-ʿIshaʾ).

al-Wahidi said: This is the view of the exegetes and the people of the language all together.

al-Farraʾ said: I heard some of the Arabs say: "Upon him is a garment dyed as if it were the shafaq," and it was red.

al-Qurtubi related this from most of the Companions, the Successors and the jurists.

Asad ibn ʿUmar and Abu Hanifah, in one of the two reports from him, said: It is whiteness. There is no basis for this view, nor any support for it, neither from the language of the Arabs nor from the Law.

al-Khalil said: "Shafaq" is the redness from the setting of the sun, and its redness at the beginning of the night until near the late night prayer. The books of language and of the Law agree upon this, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"Arise, O boy, help me, not hesitating, over time, with a cup whose filling is shafaq."

And another said:

"Of red hue like the redness of the shafaq."

Mujahid said: "Shafaq" is all of the daytime. Do you not see that He said: "and the night and what it gathers"? ʿIkrimah said: It is what remains of the daytime. They only said this because of His saying after it, "and the night and what it gathers," as if He swore by the light and the darkness. But there is no basis for this. Yet it has been related from ʿIkrimah that he said: "Shafaq" is what is between the sunset and the ʿIshaʾ. And it has been related from Asad ibn ʿUmar: "The return."

"And the night and what it gathers": "al-wasq" in the view of the people of the language is the joining of one thing to another. It is said: "istawsaqat al-ibil," when the camels gathered and came together, and "al-raʿi yasiquha," that is, he gathers them.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes say: "wa-ma wasaq" means what gathers, joins, contains and wraps. The meaning is that it gathers and joins what was scattered during the day in its activity, because when the night comes every thing returns to its shelter. From it is the saying of Dabiʾ ibn al-Harith al-Burjumi:

"So I and you, and driving toward you, are like one who grasps a thing that his fingers have not reached."

ʿIkrimah said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what drives anything to where it shelters, so he made it from "sawq" (driving), not from gathering. It was also said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what hides and covers. It was also said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what carries. Everything you carry, you have "wasaqtahu." The Arabs say: "I will not carry it, what my eye has carried of water," that is, it carried it. And the she-camel "wasaqat tasiqu wasqan," that is, carried.

Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what carries of darkness, or carries of the stars.

al-Qushayri said: The meaning of "hamala" is gathering and joining, and the night by its darkness carries every thing.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what is done in it of night prayer and seeking forgiveness at dawn. The first is preferable.

﴿And the moon when it becomes full﴾, that is, it gathers and is complete.

al-Farraʾ said: Its "ittisaq" is its becoming full, its gathering and its evening out, on the thirteenth and fourteenth night until the sixteenth. It is derived from "al-wasq," which is gathering.

al-Hasan said: "Ittasaqa" means it became full and gathered.

Qatadah said: It became round. It is said: "wasaqtuhu fa-ittasaq," as it is said: "wasaltuhu fa-ittasal" (I joined him and he became joined). And it is said: "amr fulan muttasiq," that is, gathered and ordered. And it is said: "ittasaqa al-shayʾ" when it follows in succession.

﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾: this is the answer to the oath.

Qur'an 84:19 is read with a fatha on the ba' (la-tarkabanna) by Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr, as addressed to one person, namely the Prophet ﷺ, or to anyone who is fit for it. This is also the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Masruq, Abu Wa'il, Mujahid, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. The rest read it with a damma on the ba', as addressed to the plural, meaning mankind.

al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: "La-tarkabanna, O Muhammad, sama'an ba'da sama'in" (you will ascend heaven after heaven). al-Kalbi said: "It means you will climb through them." This is according to the first reading. It was also said: a rank after a rank and a station after a station in nearness to Allah and elevation of status. It was also said that the meaning is: you will pass through state after state, each state resembling its sister in severity. It was also said that the meaning is: O human being, you will pass through state after state, from being a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then living and dead, and rich and poor. In this case the address is to the human being mentioned in His words, ﴿O mankind, indeed you are labouring toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾ (84:6). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose the second reading. They said: "Because the meaning concerning mankind is more fitting than the meaning concerning the Prophet ﷺ."

'Umar read "la-yarkabanna" with a ya' at the beginning and a damma on the ba', as a report. It is narrated from him and from Ibn 'Abbas that they read it in the third person with a fatha on the ba', meaning la-yarkabanna al-insanu (mankind will pass through). It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas that they read the prefix vowel with a kasra, and this is a dialectal form. It was also read with a fatha on the prefix and a kasra on the ba', as addressed to the self (nafs).

It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: the moon will pass through states of waning and of new crescent. This is far-fetched.

Muqatil said: "tabaqan 'an tabaq" means death and life.

'Ikrimah said: a suckling infant, then a weaned child, then a youth, then a young man, then an old man.

The position of 'an tabaq in the accusative is either as a description of tabaqan, meaning a stage passing beyond another stage, or as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the pronoun in la-tarkabanna, meaning passing beyond, or passing beyond one another.

﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ (84:20). The interrogative is for denial, and the fa' (so) indicates the sequence of the denial and astonishment that follows what precedes it, concerning the events of the Day of Resurrection or other matters, according to the earlier disagreement. The meaning is: what is the matter with the disbelievers that they do not believe in Muhammad ﷺ and in what he brought of the Qur'an, when the causes of belief in it are present?

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate﴾ (84:21). This conditional clause and its response are in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). The meaning is: what prevents them, at the time of not prostrating and humbling themselves when the Qur'an is recited?

al-Hasan, 'Ata', al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: "What is wrong with them that they do not pray?"

Abu Muslim said: the intended meaning is humility and submission.

It was also said that the intended meaning is the prostration itself known as the prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawah).

There has been disagreement as to whether this place is one of the places of prostration during recitation or not. The evidence for prostration was already mentioned at the beginning of this surah.

﴿Rather, those who disbelieve deny﴾ (84:22). That is, they deny Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought of the Book, which includes affirmation of monotheism, resurrection, reward and punishment.

﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾ (84:23). That is, of what they hide within themselves of denial. Muqatil said: they conceal some of their deeds.

Ibn Zayd said: they gather good and bad deeds. It is derived from the wi'a (receptacle) in which what is within it is gathered. From this is the poet's saying:

"Goodness endures, though time be long upon it,
and evil is the worst of what you store as provision."

It is said: wa'a means he preserved it, and I heard the hadith (wa'aytu al-hadith a'ihi wa'yan), and from this is ﴿an attentive ear﴾ (69:12).

﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (84:24). That is, treat that as glad tidings for them, because His knowledge, glorified is He, of that in the manner mentioned necessitates their punishment. The painful (alim) is that which causes pain and is afflicting. The statement is in the form of mockery toward them.

﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted﴾ (84:25). This exception is disjunctive (istithna' munqati'). That is, but those who combine belief in Allah with righteous action, for them is a reward with Allah that is not cut off (ghayr mamnun), that is, not severed. It is said: manantu al-habl, meaning I cut the rope. From this is the poet's saying:

"You see behind them, from the speed of the camels, dust like the scattering of motes."

al-Mubarrad said: al-manin is dust, because it cuts through the air behind them. Every weak thing is manin and mamnun. It was also said that the meaning of ghayr mamnun is that it is not bestowed upon them as a favour. It is permissible for the exception to be connected (muttasil) if what is meant is those among them who believed.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib concerning His words, ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ (84:1), that he said: the sky splits from the Milky Way.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿And it has listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ (84:2) that he said: it heard when He spoke to it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also concerning ﴿And it has listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ that he said: it obeyed, and it was obligated by obedience.

al-Hakim narrated from him and declared it sound, that he said: it heard and obeyed. ﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾ (84:3): he said: on the Day of Resurrection, and it casts out what is in it: he said: it brings out what is in it of the dead and empties itself of them.

Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him concerning ﴿and casts out what is in it﴾ that he said: the gold bracelets.

al-Hakim narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a good chain, from Jabir who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The earth will be stretched out on the Day of Resurrection like the stretching of a hide, and then there will be for the son of Adam in it only the place of his two feet."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with toil﴾ (84:6) that he said: one who works a deed and will encounter it; he said: one who will encounter your deed.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from 'A'ishah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one is called to account but he will be destroyed." I said: "Does Allah not say: ﴿Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾ ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾ (84:7–8)?" He said: "That is not the reckoning, but that is the presentation (al-'ard). Whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be destroyed."

Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh (p. 1603) narrated from 'A'ishah who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say in some of his prayer: 'O Allah, call me to a light account.' When he finished, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the light account?' He said: 'That he looks into his record and He overlooks it for him. Indeed whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be destroyed.'" In some wordings of the first hadith and this other hadith: "Whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be punished."

al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Bayhaqi and al-Hakim narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Three whoever has them, Allah will call him to a light reckoning and admit him to Paradise by His mercy: you give to one who withholds from you, you pardon one who wronged you, and you join one who cut you off."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿He called out for destruction﴾ (84:11), that he said: the woe (al-wayl).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him concerning His words, ﴿that he thought he would never return﴾ (84:14), that he said: he will be resurrected.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him concerning ﴿that he would never return﴾, that he said: that he would never go back.

Sammawayh narrated in his Fawa'id from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: "al-Shafaq" is the redness.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated the same from Ibn 'Abbas.

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: "al-Shafaq" is the whole of the day.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿And by the night and what it gathers (wa sa)﴾ (84:17), that he said: what enters into it.

Abu 'Ubayd in his Fada'il, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him concerning ﴿wa sa﴾ that he said: what it gathers.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also concerning His words, ﴿And by the moon when it becomes full (ittasaqa)﴾ (84:18), that he said: when it becomes equal (istawa).

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Anbari narrated through several chains from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about His words, ﴿And by the night and what it gathers﴾, and he said: what it gathers. Have you not heard the saying of the poet:

"Indeed we have she-camels, fat and spirited,
gathering together, if only they found a driver."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from him concerning ﴿And by the moon when it becomes full﴾ that he said: the night of the thirteenth.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab concerning ﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾ (84:19): state after state. al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾: state after state. He said: this is your Prophet ﷺ.

Abu 'Ubayd in al-Qira'at, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Mani', 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite "la-tarkabanna tabaqan 'an tabaq", meaning with a fatha on the ba' of tarkabanna.

He also said: meaning your Prophet ﷺ, state after state.

al-Tayalisi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated from him that he said: "la-tarkabanna", O Muhammad, the sky, stage after stage.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, al-Tabarani, Ibn Manda and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited "la-tarkabanna", meaning with a fatha on the ba'.

He also said: la-tarkabanna, O Muhammad, sama'an ba'da sama'in (heaven after heaven).

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from him concerning ﴿la-tarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: he said: meaning the sky will be split, then torn, then reddened.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from him also concerning the verse, that he said: the sky will be like molten metal (al-muhl), and it will be like red rose, like oil (al-dihan), and it will be fragile, and it will be split open, so it will be state after state.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾, that he said: they keep it secret.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 84, verses 1–25 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan without any disagreement.

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Surat al-Inshiqaq was revealed at Mecca."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn al-Zubayr something similar.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others related from Abu Rafiʿ, who said: "I prayed with Abu Hurayrah the ʿatamah (night prayer), and he recited ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and prostrated. I said to him about it, and he said: 'I prostrated behind Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ), and I will not cease to prostrate in it until I meet him.'"

Muslim, the authors of the Sunan and others related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "We prostrated with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾" [i.e., Surat al-ʿAlaq].

Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Ruwayani in his Musnad, and al-Diya al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtarah related from Buraydah that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the noon prayer ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ and similar to it."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ is like His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ (al-Takwir: 1) regarding the presence and absence of an implied verb.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: Its splitting is one of the signs of the Resurrection, and the meaning of its splitting is its cleaving with white clouds, as in His saying ﴿And the day the sky is split open with clouds﴾ (al-Furqan: 25). It was also said that it splits from the Milky Way, and the Milky Way is a gate of the sky.

The answer (jawab) of ("idha") has been disputed. al-Farraʾ said that it is "adhinat" (listened), and the waw is extra, and likewise "alqat" (cast out).

Ibn al-Anbari said: This is an error, because the Arabs do not insert the waw except with "hatta idha", as in His saying ﴿until, when they came to it and its gates were opened﴾ (al-Zumar: 73), and with "lamma", as in His saying ﴿So when they had both submitted and he had put him down upon his temple﴾ and ﴿And We called to him﴾ (al-Saffat: 103–104). It is not inserted with other than these two.

It was also said that the answer is His saying "fa-mulaqihi," meaning "then you will meet it," and this was the view of al-Akhfash.

al-Mubarrad said: In the speech there is a transposition: that is, ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor and will meet Him﴾ ﴿When the sky is split open﴾.

al-Mubarrad also said: The answer is His saying ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾, and this was the view of al-Kisaʾi. The estimate is: ﴿When the sky is split open﴾, then whoever is given his record in his right hand, his ruling is such-and-such. It was also said that it is "O mankind" with an implied "fa" (then). It was said that it is "O mankind" with an implied "qawl" (saying): that is, it is said to him, "O mankind." It was also said that the answer is omitted, its estimate being (you will be resurrected), or (every human will meet his deed). It was also said that it is what was explicitly stated in Surat al-Takwir: that is, ("a soul will know this"), on the assumption that "idha" is conditional. It was also said that it is not conditional, and is in the accusative governed by an omitted verb, meaning: remember. Or it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is the second "idha," and the waw is extra, its estimate being: the time of the splitting of the sky is the time of the stretching of the earth.

The meaning of ﴿and it has listened to its Lord﴾ is that it obeyed Him in splitting, from "idhn," which is listening to a thing and giving ear to it. ﴿And it has been right to do so﴾ means: it is right for it to obey, submit and listen. Among the uses of "idhn" in the sense of listening is the saying of the poet:

"Deaf when they hear good spoken of me, and if I am mentioned with evil in their presence, they listen (adhinu)."

And the saying of another:

"If they listen to a suspicion, they fly with it, rejoicing at me; and if they listen to something righteous, they are buried."

It was also said that the meaning is: Allah made it obligatory upon it to listen to His command to split: that is, He made it deserving of that.

al-Dahhak said: "Haqqat" means it obeyed, and it is right for it to obey its Lord because He created it. It is said: "So-and-so is entitled (mahquq) to such-and-such." The meaning of its obedience is that it does not refuse what Allah wills for it.

Qatadah said: "Haqqa laha" means it is right for it to do that. From this is the saying of Kuthayyir:

"If there is reproach, then welcome and well-come; and reproach has been due to them with us, and has become little."

And ﴿when the earth is stretched out﴾, that is, spread out as hides are spread, and its mountains are leveled until it becomes a smooth plain in which you see no crookedness or elevation.

Muqatil said: It is made level like the stretching of a hide, so no building and no mountain remains upon it except that it enters into it. It was also said: "Maddat" means it is increased in its extent, from "madad," which is increase.

﴿And it casts out what is within it﴾, that is, it brings out what is in it of the dead and the treasures, and throws them onto its surface, and empties itself of that.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: It casts out what is in its belly of the dead, and empties itself of those who are on its back of the living. A similar thing is His saying ﴿And the earth will bring forth its burdens﴾ (al-Zalzalah: 2).

﴿And it has listened to its Lord﴾, that is, it heard and obeyed in what He commanded it of casting out and emptying, and ﴿it has been right to do so﴾, that is, it was made deserving of listening to that and submitting to it. The meanings of the two verbs have already been explained before this.

﴿O mankind﴾: the intended meaning is the species of mankind, so it includes the believer and the disbeliever. It was also said that it means the disbelieving human. The first is preferable because of what follows of the detail. ﴿Indeed, you are laboring toward your Lord with labor﴾. "Kadh" in the speech of the Arabs means striving at a thing with effort, without distinction whether that thing is good or evil. The meaning is: indeed you are striving toward your Lord in your deeds, or toward meeting your Lord. It is derived from "kadaha jildahu," when he scratched his skin.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"Time is but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek life, laboring."

Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: "Workers for your Lord with a deed, and you will meet it," meaning: you will meet your deed. The meaning is that he will inevitably meet the reward of his deed and what follows from it of reward and punishment.

al-Qutaybi said: The meaning of the verse is: indeed you are laboring, that is, a worker toiling in your livelihood, toward the meeting with your Lord. "Mulaqah" means "liqa," that is, you will meet your Lord with your deed. It was also said: "fa-mulaqin kitaba ʿamalika" (you will meet the record of your deed), because the deed has already ended.

﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾: and they are the believers.

﴿He will be judged with an easy account﴾, without any scrutiny.

Muqatil said: Because his sins will be forgiven and he will not be called to account for them.

The exegetes said: It is that his sins are presented to him, then Allah forgives them, and that is the easy account.

﴿And he will return to his family in joy﴾: that is, after the easy account he will turn to his family who are in Paradise from among his kin, or to his family who were with him in the world of wives and children and who had preceded him to Paradise, or to those whom Allah prepared for him in Paradise of the wide-eyed houris and the everlasting youths, or to all of these, rejoicing, delighted with what he was given of good and honor.

﴿But as for he who is given his record behind his back﴾. al-Kalbi said: Because his right hand is chained to his neck, and his left hand will be behind him.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: The plates of his chest and his bones will be unlocked, then his hand will enter and come out from his back, and he will take his record in that manner.

﴿He will call for destruction﴾: that is, when he reads his record he will say: "Woe to me! Destruction to me!" And "thubur" means ruin.

﴿And he will burn in the Blaze﴾: that is, he will enter it and endure its heat and its severity.

Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah and ʿAsim read with a fatha on the ya and a sukun on the sad and a light lam.

The rest read with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the lam with a shadda. Ismaʿil al-Makki related from Ibn Kathir, and likewise Kharijah from Nafiʿ, and likewise Ismaʿil al-Makki related from Ibn Kathir that they read with a damma on the ya and a sukun on the sad, from "asla, yuslee."

﴿Indeed, he was among his people in joy﴾: that is, he was among his people in the world, rejoicing in following his desires and riding his lust, insolent and exultant, because the Hereafter did not occur to his mind. The clause is an explanation of what precedes it.

The clause ﴿Indeed, he thought that he would never return﴾ is an explanation of his being joyful among his people in the world. The meaning: the cause of that joy was his thinking that he would not return to Allah and would not be raised for reckoning and punishment, because he denied the resurrection and rejected the Hereafter. In His saying "an lan yahur," "an" is the light form of the heavy one, and together with what follows it fills the place of the two objects of "thanna." "Hawr" in the language means returning. It is said: "haara yahuru," when he returned. al-Raghib said: "Hawr" is hesitation in a matter, and from it: "We seek refuge in Allah from hawr after kawr," that is, from hesitation in a matter after proceeding in it. "Muhawarat al-kalam" is reviewing the speech, and "mahar" is the return and destination.

ʿIkrimah and Dawud ibn Abi Hind said: "Yahur" is a word in Abyssinian, and its meaning is "he returns."

al-Qurtubi said: "Hawr" in the speech of the Arabs means return, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hawr after kawr," meaning from returning to deficiency after increase. Likewise "hur" with a damma. In the proverb: "hur fi mahar," that is, a deficiency upon a deficiency. From it is the saying of the poet:

"The blood is shed, and the people's returner is in hur."

"Hur" also means destruction, and from it is the saying of the rajiz:

"In a well without hur he traveled, and he did not perceive."

Abu ʿUbaydah said: That is, in a well of hur, and "la" is extra.

﴿Yes, indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him﴾. "Bala" is an affirmation of the negated with "lan": that is, yes, he will surely return and will surely be raised.

Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him, that is, He was knowing of him and of his deeds, nothing of them hidden from Him.

al-Zajjaj said: "Kana bihi basiran" means He was knowing of him before He created him, knowing that his return would be to Him.

﴿So I swear by the twilight﴾: "la" is extra, as was mentioned before in similar expressions, and we have already mentioned the disagreement about it in Surat al-Qiyamah, so return to it. "Shafaq" is the redness that is after the setting of the sun until the time of the late night prayer (al-ʿIshaʾ).

al-Wahidi said: This is the view of the exegetes and the people of the language all together.

al-Farraʾ said: I heard some of the Arabs say: "Upon him is a garment dyed as if it were the shafaq," and it was red.

al-Qurtubi related this from most of the Companions, the Successors and the jurists.

Asad ibn ʿUmar and Abu Hanifah, in one of the two reports from him, said: It is whiteness. There is no basis for this view, nor any support for it, neither from the language of the Arabs nor from the Law.

al-Khalil said: "Shafaq" is the redness from the setting of the sun, and its redness at the beginning of the night until near the late night prayer. The books of language and of the Law agree upon this, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"Arise, O boy, help me, not hesitating, over time, with a cup whose filling is shafaq."

And another said:

"Of red hue like the redness of the shafaq."

Mujahid said: "Shafaq" is all of the daytime. Do you not see that He said: "and the night and what it gathers"? ʿIkrimah said: It is what remains of the daytime. They only said this because of His saying after it, "and the night and what it gathers," as if He swore by the light and the darkness. But there is no basis for this. Yet it has been related from ʿIkrimah that he said: "Shafaq" is what is between the sunset and the ʿIshaʾ. And it has been related from Asad ibn ʿUmar: "The return."

"And the night and what it gathers": "al-wasq" in the view of the people of the language is the joining of one thing to another. It is said: "istawsaqat al-ibil," when the camels gathered and came together, and "al-raʿi yasiquha," that is, he gathers them.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes say: "wa-ma wasaq" means what gathers, joins, contains and wraps. The meaning is that it gathers and joins what was scattered during the day in its activity, because when the night comes every thing returns to its shelter. From it is the saying of Dabiʾ ibn al-Harith al-Burjumi:

"So I and you, and driving toward you, are like one who grasps a thing that his fingers have not reached."

ʿIkrimah said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what drives anything to where it shelters, so he made it from "sawq" (driving), not from gathering. It was also said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what hides and covers. It was also said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what carries. Everything you carry, you have "wasaqtahu." The Arabs say: "I will not carry it, what my eye has carried of water," that is, it carried it. And the she-camel "wasaqat tasiqu wasqan," that is, carried.

Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what carries of darkness, or carries of the stars.

al-Qushayri said: The meaning of "hamala" is gathering and joining, and the night by its darkness carries every thing.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "wa-ma wasaq" means what is done in it of night prayer and seeking forgiveness at dawn. The first is preferable.

﴿And the moon when it becomes full﴾, that is, it gathers and is complete.

al-Farraʾ said: Its "ittisaq" is its becoming full, its gathering and its evening out, on the thirteenth and fourteenth night until the sixteenth. It is derived from "al-wasq," which is gathering.

al-Hasan said: "Ittasaqa" means it became full and gathered.

Qatadah said: It became round. It is said: "wasaqtuhu fa-ittasaq," as it is said: "wasaltuhu fa-ittasal" (I joined him and he became joined). And it is said: "amr fulan muttasiq," that is, gathered and ordered. And it is said: "ittasaqa al-shayʾ" when it follows in succession.

﴿You will surely ride from stage to stage﴾: this is the answer to the oath.

Qur'an 84:19 is read with a fatha on the ba' (la-tarkabanna) by Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr, as addressed to one person, namely the Prophet ﷺ, or to anyone who is fit for it. This is also the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Masruq, Abu Wa'il, Mujahid, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. The rest read it with a damma on the ba', as addressed to the plural, meaning mankind.

al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: "La-tarkabanna, O Muhammad, sama'an ba'da sama'in" (you will ascend heaven after heaven). al-Kalbi said: "It means you will climb through them." This is according to the first reading. It was also said: a rank after a rank and a station after a station in nearness to Allah and elevation of status. It was also said that the meaning is: you will pass through state after state, each state resembling its sister in severity. It was also said that the meaning is: O human being, you will pass through state after state, from being a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then living and dead, and rich and poor. In this case the address is to the human being mentioned in His words, ﴿O mankind, indeed you are labouring toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾ (84:6). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose the second reading. They said: "Because the meaning concerning mankind is more fitting than the meaning concerning the Prophet ﷺ."

'Umar read "la-yarkabanna" with a ya' at the beginning and a damma on the ba', as a report. It is narrated from him and from Ibn 'Abbas that they read it in the third person with a fatha on the ba', meaning la-yarkabanna al-insanu (mankind will pass through). It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas that they read the prefix vowel with a kasra, and this is a dialectal form. It was also read with a fatha on the prefix and a kasra on the ba', as addressed to the self (nafs).

It was also said that the meaning of the verse is: the moon will pass through states of waning and of new crescent. This is far-fetched.

Muqatil said: "tabaqan 'an tabaq" means death and life.

'Ikrimah said: a suckling infant, then a weaned child, then a youth, then a young man, then an old man.

The position of 'an tabaq in the accusative is either as a description of tabaqan, meaning a stage passing beyond another stage, or as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the pronoun in la-tarkabanna, meaning passing beyond, or passing beyond one another.

﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾ (84:20). The interrogative is for denial, and the fa' (so) indicates the sequence of the denial and astonishment that follows what precedes it, concerning the events of the Day of Resurrection or other matters, according to the earlier disagreement. The meaning is: what is the matter with the disbelievers that they do not believe in Muhammad ﷺ and in what he brought of the Qur'an, when the causes of belief in it are present?

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate﴾ (84:21). This conditional clause and its response are in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). The meaning is: what prevents them, at the time of not prostrating and humbling themselves when the Qur'an is recited?

al-Hasan, 'Ata', al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: "What is wrong with them that they do not pray?"

Abu Muslim said: the intended meaning is humility and submission.

It was also said that the intended meaning is the prostration itself known as the prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawah).

There has been disagreement as to whether this place is one of the places of prostration during recitation or not. The evidence for prostration was already mentioned at the beginning of this surah.

﴿Rather, those who disbelieve deny﴾ (84:22). That is, they deny Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought of the Book, which includes affirmation of monotheism, resurrection, reward and punishment.

﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾ (84:23). That is, of what they hide within themselves of denial. Muqatil said: they conceal some of their deeds.

Ibn Zayd said: they gather good and bad deeds. It is derived from the wi'a (receptacle) in which what is within it is gathered. From this is the poet's saying:

"Goodness endures, though time be long upon it,
and evil is the worst of what you store as provision."

It is said: wa'a means he preserved it, and I heard the hadith (wa'aytu al-hadith a'ihi wa'yan), and from this is ﴿an attentive ear﴾ (69:12).

﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (84:24). That is, treat that as glad tidings for them, because His knowledge, glorified is He, of that in the manner mentioned necessitates their punishment. The painful (alim) is that which causes pain and is afflicting. The statement is in the form of mockery toward them.

﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted﴾ (84:25). This exception is disjunctive (istithna' munqati'). That is, but those who combine belief in Allah with righteous action, for them is a reward with Allah that is not cut off (ghayr mamnun), that is, not severed. It is said: manantu al-habl, meaning I cut the rope. From this is the poet's saying:

"You see behind them, from the speed of the camels, dust like the scattering of motes."

al-Mubarrad said: al-manin is dust, because it cuts through the air behind them. Every weak thing is manin and mamnun. It was also said that the meaning of ghayr mamnun is that it is not bestowed upon them as a favour. It is permissible for the exception to be connected (muttasil) if what is meant is those among them who believed.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib concerning His words, ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ (84:1), that he said: the sky splits from the Milky Way.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿And it has listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ (84:2) that he said: it heard when He spoke to it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also concerning ﴿And it has listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ that he said: it obeyed, and it was obligated by obedience.

al-Hakim narrated from him and declared it sound, that he said: it heard and obeyed. ﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾ (84:3): he said: on the Day of Resurrection, and it casts out what is in it: he said: it brings out what is in it of the dead and empties itself of them.

Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated from him concerning ﴿and casts out what is in it﴾ that he said: the gold bracelets.

al-Hakim narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a good chain, from Jabir who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The earth will be stretched out on the Day of Resurrection like the stretching of a hide, and then there will be for the son of Adam in it only the place of his two feet."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with toil﴾ (84:6) that he said: one who works a deed and will encounter it; he said: one who will encounter your deed.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from 'A'ishah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one is called to account but he will be destroyed." I said: "Does Allah not say: ﴿Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand﴾ ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾ (84:7–8)?" He said: "That is not the reckoning, but that is the presentation (al-'ard). Whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be destroyed."

Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh (p. 1603) narrated from 'A'ishah who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say in some of his prayer: 'O Allah, call me to a light account.' When he finished, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the light account?' He said: 'That he looks into his record and He overlooks it for him. Indeed whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be destroyed.'" In some wordings of the first hadith and this other hadith: "Whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning will be punished."

al-Bazzar, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Bayhaqi and al-Hakim narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Three whoever has them, Allah will call him to a light reckoning and admit him to Paradise by His mercy: you give to one who withholds from you, you pardon one who wronged you, and you join one who cut you off."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, ﴿He called out for destruction﴾ (84:11), that he said: the woe (al-wayl).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him concerning His words, ﴿that he thought he would never return﴾ (84:14), that he said: he will be resurrected.
